html:
The K'asho Got'ine are a Dene people of the lower Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories of Canada, centred on Fort Good Hope just south of the Arctic Circle. They are part of the Sahtu Dene and speak a form of North Slavey, an Athabaskan language. Older books call them the Hare Indians, because snowshoe hares were a staple food.

They hunted caribou and moose, snared hares and fished the river. In 1805 the North West Company built a trading post at Fort Good Hope, which later passed to the Hudson's Bay Company. Its mission church, painted inside by an Oblate priest in the 1800s, is a national historic site. In 1993 the Sahtu signed a land claim agreement with Canada.
